rows.annotation: MgtC/SapB/SrpB/YhiD-family integral inner membrane protein containing DUF4010, substrate undetermined.
rows.evidence: Query domains identify an MgtC/SapB/SrpB/YhiD N-terminal domain and DUF4010; query topology predicts 13 transmembrane helices and no signal peptide. A 34.3%-identity Pseudomonas aeruginosa homolog has experimental colistin-resistance phenotypes, but no defined molecular activity. Recurrent universal-stress-protein neighbors provide contextual support only. No substrate-specific fitness measurements or biochemical transport assays are supplied.
rows.reasoning_trace: Tier B: domain assignments and homologs support a membrane-protein family, but no characterized homolog establishes a specific molecular activity or substrate. STRING provides a predicted magnesium-transport family label at 90% identity, while a 30.3%-identity comparative homolog suggests peptide transport; neither establishes substrate specificity. Specific magnesium transport, Sap peptide uptake, and colistin resistance were therefore excluded from the function statement.

[[BEGIN SUMMARY]]
%Identity to query protein: 34.30
Homolog originates from: Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1
Evidence type: experimental
This gene, encoding a hypothetical protein, was found to have mutations (Trp4Arg and Gly35Stop) in colistin-resistant P5R mutants. The Trp4Arg substitution was preserved in the colistin-susceptible revertant P5R-rev. Gene knock-out and complementation experiments using the resistant allele showed increased colistin resistance compared to the wild-type strain.
[[END SUMMARY]]

rows.conservation_breadth:
[[BEGIN CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
Counted over EVERY homolog found for this query, before the per-source display caps that apply to the other evidence blocks.
Distinct organisms with a homolog: 16 (in 11 genera)
Query organism: Pseudomonas putida
Organisms OTHER than the query's own with a homolog: 16 (10 genera other than Pseudomonas)
%Identity to query across these homologs: 30.2-50.7
Meaning: breadth of conservation, not function. A homolog in an organism other than the query's own is evidence the protein is real and under selection even when no function can be named, and supports calling it a CONSERVED hypothetical protein; homologs confined to the query's own organism do not. More organisms and more genera mean broader conservation. This NEVER constrains the specific function.
[[END CONSERVATION BREADTH]]
